resumen: Cambio de tiempos: si el verbo de reporte está en pasado, el tiempo retrocede un paso: 'I'm tired' → She said she was tired. También will → would, can → could, have done → had done. Si lo dicho sigue siendo cierto, puede quedarse en presente.

Pronombres, tiempo y lugar: cambian según quién reporta y cuándo: my → his/her, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before, here → there: He said he would call her the next day.
Say / tell: tell lleva a la persona sin preposición (She told me that...); say no (She said that..., She said to me that...). Nunca said me ni explained me.

Preguntas indirectas: orden de afirmación y sin do/does/did: She asked me where I lived. Las de sí o no llevan if o whether: He asked if I had finished. Delante de un infinitivo, solo whether: She asked whether to bring anything.
Órdenes y peticiones: tell/ask + persona + (not) to + infinitivo: She told me to wait. He asked me not to tell anyone.
Verbos de reporte + to: promise y refuse van con to; advise y warn, con persona + to: He refused to sign. She advised me to rest. They warned us not to go.

Verbos de reporte + -ing: suggest, deny, accuse of, apologise for, insist on: He denied copying it. She accused him of lying. He insisted on paying. Suggest también admite that: She suggested that we leave early.
Deny / refuse: deny niega un hecho (He denied taking it: dice que no lo tomó); refuse es negarse a hacer algo (He refused to sign: no quiso firmar).

preguntas.q: She ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
preguntas.x: Tell lleva a la persona directamente: told me that.... Say no admite a la persona sin to (said to me), y explain tampoco: se dice explained to me, no explained me.

preguntas.q: Before the guests arrived, my mum told me ___ my room.
preguntas.x: Una orden se reporta con tell + persona + to + infinitivo: told me to tidy. Con that haría falta un modal (told me that I had to tidy), y el verbo solo o con -ing no es posible.

preguntas.q: Last Monday Lucía said, 'I'm working from home today.' → Lucía said she ___ from home that day.
preguntas.x: Con el verbo de reporte en pasado, el presente continuo pasa a pasado continuo (I'm working → she was working) y today pasa a that day. Is working no sirve porque ese lunes ya pasó.

preguntas.a: Could you tell me where the nearest pharmacy is?
d: Could you tell me where is the nearest pharmacy?
Could you tell me where the nearest pharmacy it is?
Could you tell me where is it the nearest pharmacy?
preguntas.x: En una pregunta indirecta (después de Could you tell me, I wonder, She asked) se usa el orden de afirmación, sujeto + verbo: where the nearest pharmacy is. Where is the nearest pharmacy conserva el orden de la pregunta directa, y el pronombre it sobra.

preguntas.q: On Monday Carlos told Ana, 'I'll call you tomorrow.' On Wednesday Ana complained that Carlos had said he would call ___.
preguntas.x: En estilo indirecto cambian los pronombres según quién reporta (you → her) y las referencias de tiempo cuando ese día ya pasó: tomorrow → the next day. Dicho el miércoles, tomorrow señalaría el jueves.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: 'Have you finished the report?' my boss asked me.
preguntas.a: My boss asked me if I had finished the report.
d: My boss asked me if had I finished the report.
My boss asked me that I had finished the report.
My boss asked to me if I had finished the report.
preguntas.x: Las preguntas de sí o no se reportan con if o whether y orden de afirmación: asked me if I had finished. No se invierte el verbo, ask no va con that y lleva a la persona sin to.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: 'Please don't mention the new project to anyone,' my manager said to me.
preguntas.a: My manager asked me not to mention the new project to anyone.
d: My manager asked me don't mention the new project to anyone.
My manager said me not to mention the new project to anyone.
My manager asked me not mention the new project to anyone.
preguntas.x: Una petición negativa se reporta con ask + persona + not to + infinitivo: asked me not to mention. El imperativo don't mention no se conserva, y say no admite said me.

preguntas.q: At the meeting, our team leader suggested ___ the deadline to Friday.
preguntas.x: Suggest va con -ing (suggested moving) o con that + sujeto + verbo (suggested that we move). No admite to + infinitivo ni suggest us to, calco de «nos sugirió cambiar».

preguntas.q: The guide warned us ___ too close to the edge of the cliff.
preguntas.x: Warn sigue el patrón persona + (not) to + infinitivo: warned us not to go. También existe warned us against going, pero no of not going ni el imperativo dentro de la oración.

preguntas.q: When the teacher asked about the copied essay, Luis denied ___ it from the internet.
preguntas.x: Deny va con -ing (o con having + participio): denied copying, denied having copied. No admite to, aunque en español digamos «negó haberlo copiado».

preguntas.q: During the meeting, Elena accused her colleague ___ her idea.
preguntas.x: Accuse lleva of + -ing: accused her colleague of stealing. For es la preposición de blame (blamed him for), y por eso accused ... for es el error más común.

preguntas.q: The receptionist apologised ___ us waiting for so long.
preguntas.x: Apologise lleva for + -ing: apologised for keeping us waiting; a la persona se la nombra con to (apologised to us). Después de una preposición nunca va el infinitivo.

preguntas.q: We offered to split the bill, but my grandmother insisted ___ for everyone.
preguntas.x: Insist va con on + -ing (insisted on paying) o con that + oración. La preposición es on, no in, aunque en español se diga «insistir en».

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: 'No, I won't sign the new contract,' said the footballer.
preguntas.a: The footballer refused to sign the new contract.
d: The footballer denied signing the new contract.
The footballer refused signing the new contract.
The footballer denied to sign the new contract.
preguntas.x: Negarse a hacer algo es refuse to + infinitivo: refused to sign. Deny niega un hecho, así que denied signing significaría que dijo no haber firmado, no que se negó a firmar.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: 'If I were you, I'd take a few days off,' the doctor said to me.
preguntas.a: The doctor advised me to take a few days off.
d: The doctor advised me taking a few days off.
The doctor insisted me to take a few days off.
The doctor advised to me to take a few days off.
preguntas.x: If I were you, I'd... es un consejo y se reporta con advise + persona + to + infinitivo: advised me to take. Advise admite -ing solo sin persona (advised taking), e insist nunca lleva persona + to.

preguntas.q: Last year Mia told me she ___ to Scotland, so this summer I took her to Edinburgh.
preguntas.x: El present perfect (I've never been) pasa a past perfect en estilo indirecto: she had never been. Aquí el cambio es obligatorio, porque después del viaje a Edimburgo has never been ya no es verdad.

preguntas.q: Before the party, Sara asked me ___ to bring anything.
preguntas.x: Delante de un infinitivo solo se usa whether: asked me whether to bring anything. If funciona con una oración completa (asked if she should bring anything), pero no delante de to.

preguntas.a: She promised to call me as soon as she landed.
d: She suggested to take a taxi from the airport.
She refused helping us with the luggage.
She advised me going straight home.
preguntas.x: Promise va con to + infinitivo (promised to call), igual que refuse (refused to help). Suggest pide -ing o that (suggested taking), y advise con persona pide to (advised me to go).
